newsitem.title: USA: Hitachi to use U.S. Robotics modem.
newsitem.headline: Hitachi to use U.S. Robotics modem.

text.p: Hitachi PC Corp, a unit of Tokyo-based Hitachi Ltd, said Wednesday it will use U.S. Robotics' new "x2" high-speed modem technology in its notebook computers.

Terms were not disclosed, but the companies said it is the latest step in an alliance established earlier this year to integrate and brand U.S. Robotics' communications technologies with Hitachi notebook computers.
Hitachi notebooks with integrated x2 modems will begin shipping in early 1997, the company said. The computers will have attached a "Communications by U.S. Robotics" sticker logo.
Presently, Hitachi uses U.S. Robotics' modems on its C, M, E and soon-to-be-released Mx Series notebooks.

The x2 technology will allow users to download information from the Internet at speeds of 56 kilobits per second over conventional telephone lines, or almost twice as fast as today's common 28.8 kbps modem.
